topic: Inter-hospital transfer communication in mental health

audits.title: Striving for better comunication - an audit
audits.standard: All patients transferred should have a transfer letter
audits.setting: Udston Hospital, community hospital with two older adult acute mental health wards, transfers from acute site

cycle1.result: 38% transferred with medical notes, 50% with no written documentation, none with a transfer letter.

audits.intervention: Results discussed at the local clinical governance meeting; need for a transfer letter highlighted at a local management meeting.

cycle2.result: 88% had a transfer or discharge letter; 12% had no written documentation.

audits.other_findings: Sample populations differed between cycles and samples were small.
audits.citation: Breen E. Striving for better comunication - an audit. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S10-S10. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.86.

audits.title: An Audit of Information Provided to Paramedics / A&E Staff on Transfer to the Colchester General Hospital
audits.standard: PRSB Ambulance handover to emergency care standard V1.0: 100% of transfers with a doctor's support letter
audits.setting: Peter Bruff Mental Health Assessment Unit and Ardleigh Acute Inpatient Ward, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Peter Bruff: support letter in 1 of 6 transfers (17%); Ardleigh: 2 of 5 (40%).

audits.intervention: Template care summary and handover letter created
audits.citation: Zinchenko O, Shoka A, Hamza Y, Mujtaba A, Mtika V, Riding S. An Audit of Information Provided to Paramedics / A&E Staff on Transfer to the Colchester General Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S116-S117. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.332.

audits.title: Health Notes Audit
audits.standard: Complete physical health notes on transfer (consultation records, prior physical history, complete prescription with allergies)

cycle1.result: 7/12 patients transferred with complete physical health notes; no formal verbal or written physical health handover.

audits.other_findings: A proforma for preadmission meetings is being introduced from February 2024 with re-audit in February 2025.
audits.citation: Golding C, Sud N. Health Notes Audit. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S233-S233. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.570.

audits.title: Re-Audit of Preadmission Handover Meeting on a Medium Secure Rehabilitation Ward
audits.standard: NICE NG53 1.2.7, Trust handover policy and QNFMHS transfer handover standard

cycle1.result: Lack of a structured approach to preparing for preadmission meetings (no figures given).

cycle2.result: No difference in overall information sought before and after; updates still needed on physical and mental health and third-party safeguarding.

audits.other_findings: Using the checklist helped identify information gaps before the meeting so requests could be made in time.
audits.citation: Sud N, Ghandour Y, Harris M, Cranshaw T. Re-Audit of Preadmission Handover Meeting on a Medium Secure Rehabilitation Ward. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S169-S170. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10446.

audits.title: Audit of Admissions of Older People From a District General Hospital to Psychiatric Units Facilitated by Liaison Psychiatry Services
audits.standard: Locally agreed gold standards and transfer checklist (medical optimisation, handover, documentation, informing patient and next of kin)
audits.setting: Liaison psychiatry, district general hospital transfers to inpatient psychiatric units

cycle1.result: MHA paperwork 36/36; patient informed 40; GP discharge letter 40; medical optimisation confirmed 38. NEWS charts sent 17, oral intake records 13, DOLS paperwork 4/9. Other items 50% (26) to 90% (40).

audits.other_findings: Teaching for acute trust staff and a repeat audit planned; quality control of transfers to be added to liaison standard operating procedures.
audits.citation: Bhowmick M, Jenkinson J, Mabiala V, Kashif S. Audit of Admissions of Older People From a District General Hospital to Psychiatric Units Facilitated by Liaison Psychiatry Services. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S221-S222. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10559.

audits.title: An Extended, Trust-Wide Audit Assessing the Handover Process Between Mental Health Inpatient Services and Emergency Departments
audits.setting: 9 mental health inpatient wards across 3 locations in one trust

cycle1.result: 28 (62%) had no SBAR handover documented; 8 (28%) no discharge summary; 5 had neither; 25 (56%) returned with ward actions, 5 (20%) of which were delayed.

audits.other_findings: Extension of an earlier single-ward audit, showing improvement on previous findings (figures not reported). All but one ward identified handover problems.
audits.citation: Joy R, Elliott R, Beaumont S, Osukoya F, Khan S. An Extended, Trust-Wide Audit Assessing the Handover Process Between Mental Health Inpatient Services and Emergency Departments. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S249-S249. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10616.
